agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Rogers diffusion analysis and context-sensitive timing implications

analytical_question: What timing judgment follows from the same diffusion evidence for an aggressive B2B SaaS organization with an approved sandbox and dedicated evaluation staff?
general_et_finding: UNCHANGED from primary and conservative contrast: 2025 Stack Overflow 84% use OR intent and DORA 90% AI use at work are signals in differing respondent populations. Neither supplies a mid-size SaaS firm adopter-category denominator, S-curve or specific-workflow market share; stage unclassifiable.
application_finding: Routine reviewed test/documentation adoption at peer firms remains unmeasured. Rogers attributes: relative advantage=MIXED (potential drafting speed, local benefit not measured); compatibility=FAVORABLE conditional on approved sandbox, CI and review; complexity=MIXED (expert team helps, verification persists); trialability=FAVORABLE (isolated non-production sample with rollback); observability=FAVORABLE for trial metrics, not yet outcomes. All five are application-level hypotheses with low direct empirical support. Accelerator: equipped internal champion and reproducible team pilot (plausible); inhibitor: output trust and downstream review burden (survey signal/inference).
organization_specific_finding: Aggressive posture, funded evaluation capacity and a segregated environment justify starting a 2–4 week gated non-production experiment promptly, without implying that external diffusion is later-stage than in the other cases. Restrict proprietary data until security rules are documented; expand only following observed quality and cost evidence.

evidence.claim: 84% of Stack Overflow 2025 survey respondents used or intended to use AI development tools, up from 76% in 2024.
evidence.notes: Cannot interpret as 84% actual production deployment.

evidence.claim: DORA surveyed nearly 5,000 technology professionals and reported 90% AI use at work.
evidence.notes: Not a representative rate for the unit-test/doc task.

evidence.claim: 29% reported trust in output accuracy, compared with 40% in 2024.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Broad reported usage coexists with trust concerns.
Weak claim rejected: AI coding assistants are already early-majority in mid-size SaaS firms; sample and longitudinal denominators absent.
Actual reviewed tests/docs peer prevalence and benefit are unknown; external survey data from 2025 may require refresh.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate in respondent-level spread; low for Rogers stage and task-specific diffusion; local gains and defect impact unknown even with adequate evaluation infrastructure.
value_opportunity_implication: The funded sandbox can discover whether quality-adjusted cycle time improves earlier than a constrained firm could test, creating an information advantage if metrics are credible.
risk_governance_implication: Require secure sandbox, exclusion of unapproved data, human reviewers, test coverage, security checks and stop rules. Faster trial timing does not waive governance.
recommendation_management_implication: Engineering/platform lead may begin a 2–4 week isolated evaluation in the next month after verifying sandbox controls, with predeclared baseline and stop criteria; defer scale/final adoption to an independent cross-functional decision.
change_monitoring_triggers: Within 30 days capture defect escape, review time, test acceptance and author satisfaction relative to baseline.
Stop on confidential-data exposure or materially worse defects/rework.
Refresh 2025 evidence with new original surveys within 90 days and obtain comparable peer deployment cases.
Reassess tool policy, model changes or integration/standards shifts.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Do not estimate Rogers adopter category or peer usage rate.
Do not claim positive ROI before a quality-adjusted local pilot.
Confirm security sign-off, representative test set and reviewers before first experiment.
